messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-3: queue length spike (pending jobs 1,240). avg wait > 30m. autoscaler reported 'scale attempt failed: max_nodes_reached'. driver/runtime Xid errors rising across 6 nodes. SEV2. link: https://go/alerts/5087654321

irene: ack — paging oncall (carla) and infra. I'm on it.

liam: seeing same in grafana: gpu-util stable but pending queue keeps growing. autoscaler logs show repeated 'failed to acquire instance' from cloud provider.

maya: driver logs on flapping nodes show repeated cuda/xid 62 and oom kills. suspect driver/runtime instability is effectively reducing capacity.

devon: autoscaler attempted +8 nodes over last 18m, cloud returned quota=48 reached. We hit the project instance quota boundary.

ajay: @devon can we push a soft-scale by spinning up smaller instances with fewer gpus? also check if any pools are reservable (dedicated) we can borrow.

liam: tried adding smaller instances but the infra account has regional quota cap. raised emergency quota request with cloud (ticket CLD-98721). ETA unknown.

irene: mitigation plan: 1) isolate flapping nodes, 2) cordon+drain affected nodes, 3) evict non-prod/low-priority jobs to fallback, 4) enable CPU fallback for critical endpoints, 5) engage driver team for live patch.

sasha: started notifying customers on status page for impacted latencies and degraded throughput. minimal error rates so far but large tail latency. posting now. :warning:

ops-bot: status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5087654321 — message queued to customers.

maya: collecting driver stack traces from nodes gpn-uw2-03, gpn-uw2-11, gpn-uw2-17. logs show repeated 'Xid 62' then 'GPU process 0 killed by oom'. attaching snippet:```
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] driver: gpu0: Xid 62, channel 0x7f9, pid 23412
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23412 (gpu-runtime) total-vm:123G
```

ajay: quick command to check per-node Xid counts:```for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-pool-3 -o name); do ssh $n 'journalctl -u gpu-driver | grep Xid | wc -l && hostname'; done```

liam: starting cordon + drain on the 3 most noisy nodes now (gpn-uw2-03, gpn-uw2-11, gpn-uw2-17). will route new traffic away.

devon: autoscaler still trying to scale but failing due quota. Temp workaround: enable burst_buckets to allow existing nodes to accept more small-concurrency jobs. pushing config change now.

irene: change applied: reduced per-pod concurrency limit for non-critical queues, and bumped batch window to increase packing. should lower per-token overhead.

maya: driver team (ajay) proposing live restart of driver on flapping nodes + kernel param tweak (vm.overcommit_memory=1) to reduce OOMs. we should do one node at a time.

ajay: agreed. I'll run hot-restart on gpn-uw2-03 after cordon/drain completes. follow runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-restart.

liam: cordon/drain done for first node, jobs rescheduled to warm nodes. queue still high but growth rate slowed.

sasha: customer update posted: 'We are seeing increased latency and longer queueing in some GPU-backed workloads; mitigation in progress. Incident ref RDW-INC-20234.' :thumbsup:

irene: note for oncall: autoscaler logs show repeated error 'Scale failed: Max nodes reached' and driver logs show Xid 62 bursts. primary limiter right now is cloud quota + driver instability reducing usable nodes.

devon: filing follow-up CR for autoscaler: allow emergency override to consume spare quota from dedicated pools. ticket: RDW-TECH-4432.

carla: taking handoff for night shift at 5087654400. summary: quota hit blocking autoscale, driver Xid/OOMs on subset of nodes causing effective capacity loss; cordoned 3 nodes, live restart planned for next 2, low-priority jobs evicted, status page updated. escalate to driver team if Xid persists after restarts.

irene: post-incident immediate actions: 1) track cloud quota request CLD-98721, 2) driver hot-restart and kernel param rollout to remaining noisy nodes, 3) run full health-checks and restore node pool to normal, 4) prepare RCA focusing on why driver OOMs spiked and why autoscaler could not borrow capacity across pools.

ops-bot: incident severity lowered to SEV3 at 5087654470 - throughput stabilizing but not fully recovered.

carla: noted. creating incident follow-up ticket RDW-INC-20234 in ops board and assigning to devon (autoscaler), ajay (driver), liam (infra). will add postmortem timeline when handoff complete.

sasha: will keep customers updated on status page and Slack #customers impacted thread.

irene: thanks team — handoff complete.
